title: Input affordance parity: consistent hint/counter placement and animation across multiline, code, and number fields
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We have recurring inconsistencies in how helper text, character counters, and validation affordances are placed and animated across different input variants (single-line text field, multiline textarea, number field, and code editor wrapper). Symptoms include: counters jumping positions when transitioning from empty to typed state; helper text being pushed off-line at compact density; validation icon overlap with suffix actions on number/code inputs; and mismatched animation timing between components. These differences cause visual regressions in Product QA and make it harder for engineers to create new input variants that feel native to the system.

Goal: Define a token-driven system for affordance spacing and animation that ensures parity across input types and densities. Deliver design tokens, component specs, and a small set of implementable CSS/behavior changes that engineers can adopt in a single rollout.

Scope: TextField (single-line), Textarea (multiline), NumberField, and the CodeEditor field wrapper (used in inline settings). Not in scope: Selects, toggles, complex composite form controls, or platform-specific native inputs (mobile web / iOS native wrappers).
acceptance_criteria: Design tokens specified for helper-text gap, counter offset, validation-icon offset, and affordance animation duration (xs/s/m).
Visual specs for compact and default density demonstrating stable layouts for empty/focused/filled/invalid states for each input variant.
Engineering PR with component updates (TextField/Textarea/NumberField/CodeEditor wrapper) and Storybook stories validating parity across densities.
Automated visual snapshots added for the 6 canonical states per component (empty, focus, filled, invalid, overflow, with-suffix) and passing CI.
Accessibility review updated guidance: hint text should remain exposed to screen readers when visually collapsed; focus order unaffected by counters or suffixes.
